study_id: Lipkova et al. - 2022 - Deep learning-enabled assessment of cardiac allograft rejection from endomyocardial biopsies

eligibility.Eligibility Rationale: The study uses a deep learning model for biopsy rejection assessment in adult heart transplant recipients, but it does not report post‑transplant survival, waitlist mortality, or other required clinical outcomes.

identification_methods.Sponsorship source: BWH President’s Fund, NIH (NIGMS R35GM138216), Google Cloud Research Grant, Nvidia GPU Grant
identification_methods.Setting: Brigham and Women’s Hospital, Harvard Medical School (tertiary academic center)
identification_methods.Comments: Retrospective analysis of archival pathology slides from heart transplant patients.
identification_methods.Institution: Brigham and Women’s Hospital, Harvard Medical School
identification_methods.Dataset Source: Internal US cohort whole-slide images from Brigham and Women’s Hospital
identification_methods.Identification Notes: Included adult endomyocardial biopsies collected 2004‑2021; ACR cases 2007‑2021, AMR cases 2011‑2021, normal cases 2017‑2020; balanced normal and rejection cases.
identification_methods.AI Model Architecture: Weakly supervised multitask deep learning model with ResNet50 encoder, attention‑based multiple instance learning, three binary classifiers for ACR, AMR, Quilty B lesions and a separate grade classifier.
identification_methods.Input Variables: H&E‑stained whole‑slide images; patient‑level diagnostic labels (rejection presence, subtype, grade, Quilty B lesion).
identification_methods.Validation Method: 5‑fold cross‑validation, internal hold‑out test set (20% of US data), external validation on independent Turkish and Swiss cohorts.
identification_methods.Methods Notes: Used CLAM toolbox for preprocessing, tissue segmentation, patch extraction (256 × 256), ResNet50 feature extraction, attention pooling, cross‑entropy loss with equal task weighting, Adam optimizer (lr 2e‑4), early stopping, dropout 0.25.

population.Target Population: Heart transplant recipients undergoing endomyocardial biopsy
population.Population Notes: Retrospective analysis of archival pathology slides from three institutions (US, Turkey, Switzerland); patients not directly recruited; IRB approved with waived consent.

interventions_outcomes.Specific Algorithm Name: Cardiac Rejection Assessment Neural Estimator (CRANE), a weakly supervised multitask deep learning model with ResNet50 encoder and attention-based multiple instance learning
interventions_outcomes.Intervention Input Data Modality: H&E-stained whole-slide images (WSIs) of endomyocardial biopsies
interventions_outcomes.Temporal Handling: Static baseline data (single biopsy per patient)
interventions_outcomes.Interventions Notes: Model trained on patient-level labels using weakly supervised multitask learning to detect overall rejection, acute cellular rejection (ACR), antibody-mediated rejection (AMR), Quilty B lesions and to grade rejection; uses tissue segmentation, patch extraction, ResNet50 feature encoding, attention pooling, and separate classifiers for tasks
interventions_outcomes.Reported outcomes in study: Overall rejection detection, ACR subtyping, AMR subtyping, Quilty B lesion detection, rejection grade discrimination (low vs high)
interventions_outcomes.Outcomes Notes: Performance reported as area under the ROC curve (AUC) and accuracy for each task on internal US hold‑out set and external Turkish and Swiss cohorts
interventions_outcomes.Result data Notes: AUC for overall rejection detection = 0.962 (95% CI 0.943–0.980); ACR detection AUC = 0.958; AMR detection AUC = 0.874; Quilty B lesion detection AUC = 0.939; grade discrimination AUC = 0.833
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome group: All transplant recipients in the US hold‑out test set (336 patients)
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome Metric Definition: AUC on patient‑level predictions for overall rejection detection on a completely held‑out test cohort
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome Notes: High AUC indicates strong screening capability for detecting any rejection in post‑transplant biopsies
